transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because... everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments. But I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. And no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years. 

Two years... that's actually
Besides these beliefs about being targeted, have you ever heard voices or sounds, or seen things, that other people around you couldn't hear or see?

No, I don't... I mean, I'm not crazy. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. 

My hearing is actually really sharp, though. Like, I supervise the sales floor at my store, and I can hear a customer complaining from three aisles away. Just Tuesday, this woman was arguing with my newest cashier about a coupon that expired in 2022. People just don't read the fine print anymore, you know? It’s like they expect you to just bend the rules for them because they made a mistake. I had to walk all the way over there and explain the store policy, and she got so huffy... she just left her whole cart of decorative pillows right there in the middle of housewares. 

Took me twenty minutes to put it all back. And the velvet ones, they always catch the dust from the floor if you don't shelve them exactly right, which drives me absolutely insane because corporate is supposed to be doing a walkthrough next month, and they check everything. They even run a finger over the baseboards. I've been telling the closing shift to sweep better, but it's like talking to a brick wall with these kids today.

Aside from this situation with the bank and your job, have you generally felt, for most of your adult life, that other people—friends, family, coworkers—are likely to deceive or take advantage of you?

No, I wouldn't say that at all. I've always had good friends, and I trust my family. Like my best friend, Melissa, we've trusted each other with everything since we were getting our associate's degrees. We actually just went to this pottery painting place last weekend for her birthday. She’s a dental hygienist, and she gets these awful knots in her shoulders from leaning over people’s mouths all day. 

I keep telling her she needs to demand an ergonomic stool, but her boss is just incredibly cheap. He won't even buy the good mint-flavored paste for the cleanings anymore. He switched to this generic bubblegum flavor that the adult patients absolutely despise. I know because I go to him too, and last time I was there, I was tasting fake bubblegum for three days straight. It completely ruined my morning coffee. And I buy those really nice, expensive French roast beans—the ones where you can still see the oils on them? If you don't store them in an airtight container, they go stale so fast, but when you brew them right, it’s just the best way to start the morning. 

Anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, no. I don't think everyone is out to get me or deceive me. It's just the people involved with my house who are doing this.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that the bank, loan servicer, and coworkers are conspiring to force her from her home) that has persisted for approximately two years. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech (only tangential/circumstantial elaboration during conversation), and no negative symptoms. Her overall functioning is well preserved—she maintains steady employment as a supervisor, has long-standing close friendships, and engages in normal social activities. Her suspiciousness is circumscribed specifically to the foreclosure situation and does not generalize to a pervasive distrust of others (ruling out paranoid personality disorder), and the absence of hallucinations, disorganization, or broad functional decline argues against schizophrenia. This pattern—a single, encapsulated, non-bizarre delusional system with preserved functioning and no other psychotic features—is most consistent with Delusional Disorder, persecutory type (F22).
